notes: Sixth sweep (previous sweep ba24972): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, each result.json recording head d04061d with no uncommitted changes and skill_hash 005deae0..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder; every transcript contains the rewritten head-binding text ("A head binds what selects its clause"). result.json records skills_listed 209 for every run (the previous sweep had 16 or 29). Opus-1 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md, the other four SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all five. In the scratch folder all five pass mix format --check-formatted and run against a stand-in Decimal written there (the Hex cache has no decimal package). A probe gave correct per-currency totals, last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day in all five) and empty results for []; all five return {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status and a bad date. Haiku-2's top_customers keeps customers with zero completed orders ({"b", 0} in the probe); haiku-1 reports a missing key as :invalid_order and sonnet-2 as :missing_field without the key; no rule in the list covers these, so they are noted in the summaries only.

No rule in this case's list changed since ba24972. git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes two SKILL.md rules outside the list, "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys" (three new paragraphs) and "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" (rewritten), plus one sentence in references/ex_unit.md "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" (not exercised here). All ten listed rules are graded to the previous sweep's standard, and all ten are clean in all five runs (previous sweep: 2 of 5 broke the with rule, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 with one-step withs nesting a case; neither recurs, as parse_amount/1 and parse_placed_at/1 are now plain case functions chained as with steps in every run).

The instruction to count violations per bullet of the rewritten rules refers to evals/cases/webhook-parser.md and evals/cases/library-client.md; order-report.md's What to check list has no bullet for either rewritten rule, so the counts below are for the rewritten rules as other rules, sentence by sentence, out of 5 runs. Head binding: a field no pattern or guard uses, bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, 0; bound in a head that mix format spreads over several lines, 0 (haiku-1's parse_order/1, lines 66-72, and sonnet-2's, lines 96-104, are multi-line heads binding the five required keys, but a catch-all clause follows each, so the keys select by presence: "A head binds what selects its clause: ... a key whose presence selects, because another clause catches the input that lacks it."); a selecting pattern moved into the body, 0; a string-keyed parser that does not match its required keys in the head, 0 (opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 check each key with string_field/2 chained in a with, which "Parse external data into structs where it enters the system" names for when the caller needs the field, held clean as in the previous sweep); a catch-all naming a cause it cannot tell apart, 0 (haiku-1's :invalid_order is the rule's own shape; sonnet-2's :missing_field at line 119 is held clean because the rows are maps, so the clause only receives a map lacking a required key, and it names no particular key). Read required keys: a body pattern pulling one field out of a held value, 0; a chain bound step by step, 0; map[:key] or Map.get/2 where absent and nil differ, 0 (every lookup is a head pattern or Map.fetch/2).

Unchanged rules, same standard as the previous sweep. The with rule is decided by "Count the `<-` clauses before writing `with`." and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step": build/1's single parse call is a case in all five (opus-1 108, haiku-1 51, haiku-2 59, sonnet-1 86, sonnet-2 78); the withs have nine (opus-1), eight (haiku-2, sonnet-1) or three steps (haiku-1, sonnet-2). The Enum/Map rule is decided by "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand": 0 of 5; all group with Enum.group_by then Map.new, and opus-1 counts with frequencies_by while the others count the filtered list that also feeds the totals (Enum.count or length/1), held clean as before; the Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces. Lists: opus-1 prepends without reversing (line 119), held clean as before because nothing downstream depends on the order. The do: rule's mixed-function sentence is exercised by haiku-1's parse_order/1 and sonnet-2's parse_order/1, parse_amount/1 and parse_placed_at/1, each block clause set apart by a blank line; no do: body is wrapped onto its own line. Naming, captures, dates, money, atoms and processes: all five clean. Other rules: every public function has @doc with doctest examples, every defstruct uses @enforce_keys or bare atoms, no multi-line literal is passed as a call argument, and no case or with nests inside another; no other violation was found.
